business_problem: The NCSC needed to scale protection against DNS threats for UK public services as cyber incidents increased, while filtering large volumes of lower-severity malicious domains without disrupting essential operations.
solution_summary: The NCSC worked with Accenture and Cloudflare to implement a new Protective Domain Name Service (PDNS) platform for public-sector internet access. PDNS filters and analyzes DNS queries, acting as a real-time allow/block service that directs users only to intended websites. Cloudflare's AI neural networks analyze internet activity and, together with more than 30 threat-intelligence providers, identify malicious domains for near-real-time blocking. The partners integrated data flows, prepared more than 1,000 organizations for the change, and moved over 8 million public-sector users to the new service in a single cutover without disrupting critical operations. The platform also provides trend insights that help the NCSC understand and mitigate threats; the source does not specify storage or model-training infrastructure.

solution_components.name: Protective Domain Name Service (PDNS)
solution_components.role: Filters DNS queries and blocks malicious domains in real time for protected public-sector users.

solution_components.name: Cloudflare AI neural networks
solution_components.role: Analyze internet activity to provide near-real-time threat detection for the PDNS service.

data_flow: DNS queries from public-sector users are filtered by PDNS; Cloudflare neural networks and threat-intelligence providers identify malicious domains, and PDNS allows or blocks the requested destinations.
business_outcome: The system transitioned over 8 million public-sector users without disruption, blocked hundreds of millions of threats, and gives the NCSC a scalable way to onboard organizations and focus security teams on more critical attacks.
